query: For high-entropy alloys used in thermal-insulation applications, what testable hypothesis could be made about an unspecified predictive approach for accurately identifying materials with low phonon thermal conductivity? The hypothesis should explain why the approach would work, predict its improvement over current predictions, define its applicability limits, identify supporting evidence, and specify a decisive experimental benchmark and outcome that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: A screening approach that combines (i) first-principles–derived local atomic-mass variance (σM2) and (ii) an anharmonic bond-stiffness mismatch index (Γbond) will identify face-centered-cubic (FCC) high-entropy alloys (HEAs) with room-temperature lattice thermal conductivity κlat ≤ 1.0 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ with ≥80 % precision—roughly twice the hit-rate obtained by the current rule-of-mixtures (RoM) or average-property filters.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast, nominally equiatomic single-phase FCC high-entropy alloys composed of five transition-metal elements (≥50 amu average atomic mass) and no intentional nano-structuring.
generation.intervention: Apply the σM2 + Γbond predictive screen to a virtual library of candidate quinary FCC HEAs and synthesize the ten compositions ranked lowest in the combined descriptor.
generation.conditions: Room temperature (300 K), ambient pressure, fully dense polycrystalline bulk specimens.
generation.structural_mediator: High local mass variance and bond-stiffness contrast create strong point-defect and strain-field scattering centers for acoustic phonons throughout the random solid-solution lattice.
generation.mechanism: Large σM2 increases mass-fluctuation scattering rates while a high Γbond magnifies anharmonic three-phonon interactions; together they suppress phonon mean-free paths, lowering κlat. The descriptors capture these scattering sources more faithfully than RoM averages, yielding superior predictive power.
generation.predicted_outcome: At least 8 of the 10 screened alloys will exhibit κlat ≤ 1.0 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ (median ≈ 0.8 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹), whereas fewer than 4 of 10 alloys chosen by RoM filtering will meet the ≤ 1.0 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ target (median ≈ 1.2 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹).
generation.baseline: State-of-the-art screening based on rule-of-mixtures averages of atomic mass, Debye temperature and Grüneisen parameter yields ~40 % precision for κlat ≤ 1 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ in comparable HEAs.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is limited to single-phase FCC HEAs whose X-ray diffraction shows <5 % secondary phases and lattice-parameter variation <0.5 %. It may fail for BCC or multiphase HEAs, or for samples with significant porosity or nano-precipitates that introduce additional scattering not captured by the descriptors.
generation.uncertainty: Magnitude of improvement (≈2 × precision, ≈0.4 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ reduction in median κlat) is approximate; unforeseen processing defects or phase separation could mask the intrinsic lattice contribution.

falsification_experiment.design: 1. Use the σM2 + Γbond model to rank 1000 hypothetical equiatomic quinary FCC HEAs drawn from a 12-element transition-metal pool. 2. Synthesize the 10 top-ranked and 10 RoM-selected control alloys under identical arc-melting and homogenization schedules. 3. Verify single-phase FCC structure by XRD and SEM/EDS. 4. Measure density (Archimedes), specific heat (DSC), and thermal diffusivity (laser flash) to obtain κlat at 300 K (κlat = α·ρ·Cp, subtracting any electronic contribution estimated from four-probe resistivity).
measurements: κlat at 300 K for each alloy
Phase purity fraction from XRD Rietveld analysis
Density, Cp, α to cross-validate κlat calculation
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if fewer than 7 of the 10 descriptor-selected alloys have κlat ≤ 1.0 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ OR if a two-proportion z-test shows the precision improvement over the RoM control set is not statistically significant at p < 0.05.
